I now have the complete call chain with file:line evidence. Here is my root-cause analysis.

## Root cause chain (with evidence)

The warning fires from the `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` **`if (!parent)` guard** — the function was passed a NULL parent while trying to remove the sysfs node literally named `"typec"`:

```c
// fs/kernfs/dir.c (kernfs_remove_by_name_ns)
if (!parent) {
    WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
    return -ENOENT;
}
```

That guard is your exact message (`"kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory"` → `-ENOENT`). So the sysfs *parent directory* handed to the lookup is NULL, which means `kernfs_find_ns()`'s parent is gone.

Reading the call chain bottom-up (this tree, 6.17-based):

| Step | Location | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143` `sysfs_remove_link()` | = `parent = kobj->sd; kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name)` (lines 146-152). **`parent` is NULL iff `kobj->sd` is NULL**, i.e. the kobject lost its kernfs/sysfs node. |
| 2 | `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:910` `typec_partner_unlink_device()` | `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` removes the `"typec"` symlink that `typec_partner_link_device()` created on the USB device at `class.c:893` (`sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec")`). |
| 3 | `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1184-1186` `typec_unregister_partner()` | calls `typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev)` / `usb3_dev` when those pointers are non-NULL. |
| 4 | `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1151` `ucsi_unregister_partner()` | `typec_unregister_partner(con->partner)`. |
| 5 | `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264-1366` `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` | workqueue handler (`kworker/6:0`); on `UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE` with `CONNECTED` cleared it calls `ucsi_unregister_partner()` in the `else` branch. |

The `name == "typec"` + `parent == NULL` means `dev->kobj.sd == NULL` **for the `struct usb_device *` held in `port->usb2_dev` / `port->usb3_dev`** — that USB device has already had its sysfs/kernfs node torn down (`kobject_del()`/`device_del()`).

## Why it fails with ENOENT

`port->usb{2,3}_dev` is a stale/reference to a `stb USB device` that was removed from sysfs below the typec layer. Only ONE place owns clearing those pointers back to NULL: `typec_partner_deattach()` (`class.c:2177-2180` sets `port->usb2_dev = NULL` / `usb3_dev = NULL`), invoked from the USB hub's `usb_disconnect()`:

- `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2315` `usb_disconnect()` → at **`hub.c:2363`** `typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &udev->dev)` **before** `device_del(&udev->dev)` (`hub.c:2386`).

The race: the UCSI controller (ACPI based here, `ucsi_acpi` — Dell) observes a connector `CONNECT_CHANGE` and runs `ucsi_unregister_partner()`→`typec_unregister_partner()` on its own workqueue. `typec_unregister_partner()` **does not clear `port->usb2_dev` / `port->usb3_dev`** (compare the nulling done only in `typec_partner_deattach` at `class.c:2177-2180`). When the connector↔USB-device association on that port does not go back through `typec_partner_deattach` (the typec partner connector and the USB `usb_port` connector are separate objects — the typec side can be behind DRM, cf. `drm_sysfs.c:104 typec_connector_bind`), the pointer is never reset to NULL. A later teardown then dereferences `port->usb{2,3}_dev` that already had its sysfs node destroyed → `dev->kobj.sd == NULL` → `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(NULL, "typec")` → WARN + `-ENOENT`.

## Is a fix present in this tree?

**No driver-side fix is present.** This 6.17 snapshot still:
- contains the WARN path in `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731-1734` (it is the diagnostic, not the fix), and
- `typec_unregister_partner()` (`class.c:1174-1195`) does **not** NULL out `port->usb2_dev`/`port->usb3_dev`, leaving the stale pointer that triggers the warning. The nulling exists only on the USB-hub teardown path (`typec_partner_deattach`, `class.c:2177-2180`), so the two owners are asymmetric.

The upstream correction is exactly that driver-side hardening: on the typec/UCSI unregister path also drop/release the `port->usb_{2,3}_dev` reference and avoid unlinking when the underlying USB device's sysfs node is gone, so `sysfs_remove_link()`/`kernfs_remove_by_name()` is never called with a `dev` whose `kobj.sd` has already been dropped. Because the snapshot's `typec_unregister_partner()` still relies on the stale pointer, this warning remains reporducible on `6.17.0-1011-oem`; the fix sequence is not carried in this tree snapshot.

(Side-note: `ucsi_handle_connector_change` also contains the recent `EVENT_PENDING`/`"entered without EVENT_PENDING"` debug guard at `ucsi.c:1278-1281`, confirming stale connector-change events are a known flank of this same teardown-race class, but they guard the UCSI event loop; the actual NULL-parent WARN here is at the kernfs/sysfs layer because of the stale `port->usbX_dev`.)
